releases.summary: Initial public Kepler plugin and portable generated Hub.

changes.text: Published the neutral Kepler coordinator, focused engineering skills, setup generator, Doctor, repository bridges, and local acceptance tooling.

releases.summary: Direct GitHub marketplace installation and public plugin metadata.

changes.text: Added the direct GitHub marketplace installation path and public repository metadata.
Documented supported update, uninstall, contribution, and public-readiness workflows.

releases.summary: Visual onboarding for the repository and Codex plugin interface.

changes.text: Added an original repository hero, animated routing tour, expandable quick starts, plugin icon, brand color, and interface screenshot.

releases.summary: Natural-language setup, planning, review, CI/CD, platform, STIG, and safe plugin lifecycle workflows.

changes.text: Added one-prompt setup that discovers and connects existing repositories with safe reference bridges.
Added adaptive planning and findings-first review skills that trigger from natural intent.
Added focused CI/CD and platform skills with evidence, ownership, approval, and runtime boundaries.
Expanded STIG evaluation with evidence contracts, draft and export readiness, deterministic validation, and generated-Hub guidance.
Added a safe in-place plugin upgrade workflow, deterministic patch notes, preservation checks, and explicit rollback limits.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the new skill definitions load.
Existing generated Hubs are preserved and are not automatically migrated.

changes.text: Limited plugin default prompts to the three entries supported by Codex so setup, planning or review, and upgrade suggestions load correctly.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the corrected plugin prompts load.

releases.summary: Database engineering guidance and faster, stricter STIG workflows.

changes.text: Added the implicitly triggered kepler-db skill for database design, queries, transactions, migrations, security, performance, reliability, and operational safety.
Added quick, standard, and batch/export STIG execution modes so focused questions avoid unnecessary CKL tooling.
Prevented CKL-ready summaries from accepting unsupported decided statuses and rejected duplicate vulnerability IDs in CKL templates.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the kepler-db skill and updated STIG guidance load.
Existing generated Hubs are preserved and are not automatically migrated.

releases.summary: Outcome-led skill composition with dynamic platform and database handoffs.

changes.text: Made SSH, remote-host, kind, kubectl, live deployment, and runtime-validation requests trigger kepler-platform from natural user intent.
Selected lead and companion skills from the requested outcome instead of the owning workload, carried their exact names into child prompts, and deferred speculative skills.
Made runtime-discovered database, schema, migration-version, backfill, locking, and persistence issues load kepler-db before database action without expanding authorization.
Added deterministic validation and fresh-task acceptance coverage for platform-led chart handoffs and mid-task database escalation.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the updated skill triggers and composition rules load.
Existing generated Hubs are preserved and are not automatically migrated; updated installed skills still apply from fresh tasks.

releases.summary: Professional compliance deliverables with fail-closed presentation validation.

changes.text: Added deterministic validation for document text, Office and PDF metadata, unresolved variables, filenames, and constrained archive contents.
Separated polished compliance deliverables from internal working records and removed default customer-facing sidecars and authoring-process metadata.
Prevented AI provenance, review-workflow labels, internal STIG review fields, and unresolved template markers from leaking into final deliverables.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the professional deliverable rules and validator load.
Existing generated Hubs are preserved and are not automatically migrated; adopt the deliverables and working-records layout explicitly where needed.

releases.summary: Resilient Doctor diagnostics and explicit preserved-Hub compatibility checks.

changes.text: Prevented missing or concurrently unavailable repository paths from crashing Doctor, status, bridge inspection, or command capture; affected checks now return deterministic structured findings.

Added a versioned generated-Hub capability contract and read-only compatibility checker with exact capability probes, managed migration scope, protected user-state exclusions, and fail-closed fallback behavior.
Made setup, review, repository-bridge, and upgrade skills check the Hub capabilities they require before relying on newer commands or documents.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the updated Doctor, compatibility, and skill guidance load.
Existing generated Hubs are preserved and are not automatically regenerated or migrated.
When a required capability is unavailable, use the reported plan-and-diff migration scope; plugin upgrade alone does not modify the Hub.

changes.text: Renamed the Flightdeck product, plugin, skills, generated project, assets, links, and contracts to Kepler.
Added confirmed ArchitectureMaps, revisioned Plans, budgeted ContextPacks, exact dispatch receipts, WorkerResults, and scoped typed memory.
Made Sol responsible for planning, Terra responsible for exact one-shot dispatch, and ordinary Codex tasks responsible for execution.
Removed the operations product surface and kept Mission and Operation lifecycle control planes absent.

breaking_changes: Plugin and skill identifiers change from flightdeck to kepler.
Old command and marketplace identifiers are not compatibility aliases.
migration: Snapshot existing generated state before migration.
Install Kepler as a separate plugin identity and start a fresh Codex task.
Migrate supported declarations, confirm an ArchitectureMap, and run Doctor; connected repositories are not rewritten.

changes.text: Replaced repository-root discovery and generated workload topology with exact selection of existing saved Codex projects and a confirmed ArchitectureMap.
Made explicit /kepler commands primary, allowed Sol read-only planning inspection, bound dispatch requests to Terra, and preserved ordinary directly accessible workers.
Demoted repository bridges to optional advanced policy and made absent bridges valid while configured bridge drift still fails closed.
Added literal Git and local marketplace installation guidance plus installed-runtime evidence contracts for model identity, exact project routing, WorkerResults, and upgrade preservation.
Removed default development, charts, patching, research, environments, and compliance pseudo-workload directories and their legacy handoff helper.

breaking_changes: New control projects use project-first setup and no longer generate workload directories or install bridges during setup.
The old repository-root setup plan/connect command flow is not part of the default v1.1 interface.
migration: Preserve an existing control project as rollback evidence; install Kepler 1.1.0 and start a fresh task.
Create a new control project, select existing saved Codex projects by opaque runtime ID and exact path, confirm the ArchitectureMap, and run Doctor.
Do not copy workload lifecycle state, Missions, Operations, transcripts, or Kepler-legacy content into the new control project.

releases.summary: Single-task Sol control loop, exact worker routing, and optional Herdr execution visibility.

changes.text: Kept review-only Plans and Plan revisions in the current task when it already runs Sol with high reasoning, instead of creating a redundant control-project task.
Required every new implementation, review, research, and synthesis worker to use the permission-preserving bootstrap and final-task verification before receiving its prompt.
Rejected direct-created, mismatched, or unattested DispatchReceipts so a managed workspace sandbox cannot be recorded as inherited global configuration.
Required completed WorkerResults to be ingested before synthesis or replanning instead of copying findings into redundant planner prompts.
Kept dispatch in the current Sol control task instead of creating a redundant control-project Terra dispatcher task.

Prohibited collaboration-agent routing for repository workers, bound app-server task creation to the owning opaque project ID, and required the returned project ID and task path to remain stable after creation, handoff, prompt delivery, and continuation.
Made planner bootstrap return a no-op reuse receipt for an existing Sol High task unless the user explicitly requests a separate planner.
Reduced ContextPack memory and related-work expansion, required one-copy dispatch prompts and compact structured results, and exposed artifact-only token estimates in Plan status.
Added an optional Herdr attachment that resumes the same exact verified Codex worker in a receipt-owned terminal workspace without replacing app-server project identity or WorkerResults.

Added explicit receipt-driven cleanup that closes owned Herdr workspaces, archives completed Codex workers, and removes only clean inactive Worktrees already merged into the owning checkout while preserving branches.

migration: Start a fresh Codex task after upgrading so the updated single-control-task routing instructions and MCP tool schema load.
New generated control projects require permission-attested DispatchReceipts; existing generated control projects remain preserved.
Existing generated control projects remain valid and are not regenerated automatically.
Herdr attachment and cleanup require a newly generated or explicitly migrated control project plus a fresh Codex task started inside Herdr.

releases.summary: Desktop-independent Codex CLI dispatch and result collection in Herdr.

changes.text: Added a persistent Codex CLI project catalog plus explicitly confirmed exact-path project registration for Herdr setup.
Added ContextPack delivery through the exact attached Herdr worker with prompt hashing, duplicate suppression, and pre/post CLI task, project, path, and terminal verification.
Added final-response-only result collection for completed exact Herdr workers.
Herdr dispatch now creates each worker as an owned tab inside the current control workspace instead of creating a worker workspace.
Cleanup now previews the exact removal set and requires one explicit cleanup authorize before closing worker tabs, archiving tasks, or removing safe Worktrees.
Removed the Codex desktop app and browser-control dependency from the Herdr dispatch workflow.

migration: Start a fresh Herdr control task after upgrading so the 1.1.2 MCP tool schema loads.
Run /kepler setup in Herdr, explicitly confirm any missing exact project paths, and replace desktop-only opaque IDs with CLI project IDs.
Migrate the preserved control project to capability kepler.command.cli-herdr-dispatch.v1 before dispatch; plugin upgrade alone does not rewrite Hub state.

releases.summary: Codex CLI Terra runtime preservation during worker verification.

changes.text: Reapplied the requested worker model, reasoning effort, exact cwd, approval policy, and sandbox or permission profile when resuming an empty CLI worker for mandatory pre-prompt verification.
Prevented the CLI verifier from falling back to the Sol control-agent model before Herdr attachment.

migration: Start a fresh Herdr control task after upgrading so the Kepler 1.1.3 MCP server loads.
No generated-Hub migration is required when the Hub already declares kepler.command.cli-herdr-dispatch.v1.

releases.summary: Reliable Herdr attachment while a new worker pane settles.

changes.text: Retried only Herdr's structured agent_pane_busy response for up to five seconds while a newly created worker tab's shell becomes available.
Reused the exact tab, pane, agent name, and Codex resume arguments on retry without delivering the ContextPack early or creating another workspace.
Added allowed- and denied-path regressions for transient pane readiness and non-retryable Herdr attachment errors.

migration: Start a fresh Herdr control task after upgrading so the Kepler 1.1.4 MCP server loads.
No generated-Hub migration is required when the Hub already declares kepler.command.cli-herdr-dispatch.v1.
